title: Cain and Abel
text:
Adam and Eve had two sons. Cain, the elder, worked the soil. Abel kept flocks. In the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruits of the ground as an offering to the Lord, and Abel brought the fat portions of the firstborn of his flock.

The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but not on Cain and his. Cain was furious, and his face fell. The Lord spoke to him: why was he angry? If he did what was right, would he not be accepted? But if not, sin was crouching at the door; it desired to have him, but he must rule over it.

Cain did not master it. He said to his brother, "Let us go out to the field." And while they were in the field, Cain attacked Abel and killed him.

The Lord asked Cain where his brother was. "I do not know," Cain answered. "Am I my brother's keeper?" The Lord said that his brother's blood was crying out from the ground. Cain was cursed: the earth would no longer yield its strength to him, and he would be a restless wanderer. Cain protested that his punishment was more than he could bear, and that whoever found him would kill him. So the Lord put a mark on Cain, so that no one would kill him, and he went away and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
lesson: Envy between siblings is natural, but it must be mastered before it masters us. Notice resentment early and deal with it while it is still small.
